newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan PM greets Gujral with message of peace.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan PM greets Gujral with message of peace.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday the appintment of Inder Kumar Gujral as Indian prime minister had boosted hopes for peace.

In a congratulatory message to Gujral, who won a confidence vote in the Indian parliament earlier on Tuesday, Sharif said: "Your elevation as prime minister of India has stimulated hopes for a determined effort by both of our countries to carry forward the recently resumed dialogue.
"The success of our efforts will naturally depend on the seriousness of purpose and political 'will' with which the core issue of Jammu and Kashmir is addressed," he said.
India and Pakistan, now seen as threshold nuclear powers, have fought three wars since independence from Britain 50 years ago, two of them over the divided Himalayan region of Kashmir.

"We have been encouraged by your statements underlining your commitment to the improvement of relations between our two countries," Sharif said. "Let me assure you on my part that my government remains committed to a genuine search for peace."
Sharif said he looked forward to meeting Gujral at a South Asian regional summit in the Maldives next month.
Pakistan and India resumed talks at foreign secretary level at the end of March for the first time in more than three years.
Gujral, foreign minister under H.D. Deve Gowda, met his Pakistani counterpart Gohar Ayub at a Non-Aligned Movement meeting in New Delhi this month.
